newsitem.title: INDIA: India Finolex plans major expansions.
newsitem.headline: India Finolex plans major expansions.

text.p: India's Finolex Industries Ltd plans to boost its PVC capacity by 70,000 tonnes to 200,000 tonnes over the next two years and will borrow $30 million overseas to fund the expansion, a company official said.

"This year we are expanding 70,000 tonnes, but what we foresee is that the demand for PVC in India has to cross one million tonnes very soon," Finolex Chairman Pralhad Chhabria told Reuters in a recent interview at his headquarters in this western Indian city of Pune.
"So we are going to catch up again from 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes," Chhabria added. "Gradually we would like to increase it."
The expansion would be spread over two years -- financial year 1997/98 (april-March) and 1998/99, Chhabria said. "These two years we'll be busy expanding that area."

Set on a 120-acre site at Ratnagiri on India's west coast, Finolex's PVC resin plant will be powered by a 25 MW captive power plant that Chhabria said has been granted approval by the state government.
Finolex would raise money to fund the expansion at comparatively low rates of interest overseas, Chhabria said.

"We'll borrow the money by external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and the rate of interest in ECBs is very low," Chhabria said. "The advantage we'll get is that although interest costs have come down to between 15 and 16 percent in India, we'll be paying half the cost."
Finolex has already raised about $10 million through ECBs in financial year 1997/98 (April-March), Chhabria said.
"Now we are going for another $30 million ECB so our expansion for 70,000 tonnes and the power plant and our internal generation will be complete this year, '97/98," he added.
The expansion would have another healthy impact on the company's bottomline, Chhabria said.

"If you study the balance sheet of Finolex Industries, interest costs and power are taking away the major money. From this year onward, we'll reduce it drastically, so that there will be heavy reduction in the power bill and also the interest charge -- both will come down."

Chhabria said Finolex would commission a plant to make copper rods in Goa in October. Set up in a joint venture with Essex Industries of the U.S., the plant will have an estimated capacity of 60,000 MT annually in the first phase, rising to 80,000 MT.
